title: WireBatch
description: The request body of POST /v1/e: one batch of up to 10 events or anonymous pings (01 §6). A batch never mixes the two: it is all events, with the per-pageload batch counter seq, or all pings, without it, so that a ping is never sent beside a seq (02 §2, 08 G2). Its items carry their own schema_version.

EventBatch.description: A batch of events, sent while consent allows collection with identifiers.

seq.description: The per-pageload batch counter: 1 for a page's first batch, one more for each batch after it, retries keeping theirs, and 1 again with each new page_id. It lives in memory only, dies with the page and identifies nobody; the collector reads its gaps as lost batches (AAI-106). Every event batch carries it, so that a batch sent without it is refused rather than left out of the loss count (AAI-950).

page_id.description: The pageload's key: the same value on every batch of one pageload, retries included, and a new one on the next, and a new one when consent is granted again after a withdrawal, so that the fresh visitor id is never joined to the withdrawn one (AAI-1156), and so that the processor can link a pageload's batches and count the gaps in their seq (AAI-106). Optional only because tags up to v0.4.0 send event batches without it; this tag sends it on every event batch.

webdriver.description: Sent, as true, when the browser reports navigator.webdriver === true: it is driven by automation (WebDriver, Puppeteer, Playwright and the like). It feeds the collector's bot marking (03 §5, AAI-76) and names the browser, never the visitor. Absent otherwise: the tag never sends false. It belongs to the browser, so it goes once per batch rather than on each event. A ping batch never carries it: pings leave the browsers of visitors who declined, and their field list is frozen.

PingBatch.description: A batch of anonymous pings, sent by declined mode `pings`. It carries no seq and no page_id: pings are never sequence-linkable.

PageId.description: A random UUID, version 4, in lower-case hex: 122 random bits and no time. The tag makes it once per pageload, and again when consent is granted again after a withdrawal, and keeps it in memory only: it is never stored on the device, dies with the page and identifies nobody. Only an event batch carries it, never a PingBatch (08 G2).
